review.notes: The goat script's own header states both behaviours (restriction does not apply if the effect is negated; does not apply to immune monsters). The goat cdb text matches v0 (SOD-EN042, 2004-10-01) at 0.9774, differing only by writing the dragon's modern name 'Red-Eyes Black Dragon' where the lineage prints 'Red-Eyes B. Dragon'. The English lineage is cosmetic end to end: v0 -> v1 (DR3-EN042, 2006-11-25) drops 'Life Points' and shortens the restriction clause; v1 -> v2 (DTP1-EN015, 2008-07-24) folds the selection into the damage sentence; v2 -> v3 (SDDC-EN026, 2012-02-03) restores explicit 'Target 1'; v3 -> v4 (LEDU-EN007, 2017-09-07) is 'in your Monster Zone'; v4 -> v5 (LDS1-EN016, 2020-07-02) is the card's rename. Both scripts set EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET and select through Duel.SelectTarget, so the Select/Target wording churn is not a targeting change. The once-per-turn attack-activity gate (Duel.AddCustomActivityCounter / GetCustomActivityCount) is identical in both.

event.historical_text: Select 1 face-up "Red-Eyes B. Dragon" on your side of the field to activate this card. Inflict damage to your opponent's Life Points equal to the original ATK of the selected "Red-Eyes B. Dragon". "Red-Eyes B. Dragon" cannot attack during the turn you use this card.
event.summary: Era handling of the attack restriction, not a text erratum: the GOAT script registers the '"Red-Eyes B. Dragon" cannot attack' field effect inside s.activate, on resolution, with no EFFECT_FLAG_OATH and no EFFECT_FLAG_IGNORE_IMMUNE, while the modern script registers it inside s.cost, at activation, carrying both flags. So in the era version a negated Inferno Fire Blast imposes no attack restriction at all, and a Red-Eyes immune to this card's effects can still attack, whereas the modern card restricts regardless of negation or immunity. Damage is the target's original ATK in both. Chronology is unresolved - no source in the packet dates the change.
